disposition_reason: One cocoa powder and one hot chocolate item were analysed for Al by FAAS within the 'Coffee, Cocoa & Tea' group (Beirut market, May-Sept 2018), but the paper reports Al only at food-group level (group mean/min/max in Fig. 1; 'Coffee, Cocoa and Tea (6.36)' in text) mixed with coffee and tea; no cocoa-specific concentration is printed. Table 3 gives only consumption/ingestion rates for cocoa powder (100 g portion, 6.84 g/day) and packaging contact.
disposition_locator: Section 2.3.5 Food groups; Table 3 (group 7, rows 'Hot chocolate (1)' and 'Cocoa powder (1)'); Fig. 1; Results p.1027-1028

study.design: market survey with food-frequency exposure assessment
study.material_scope: cocoa powder (1 item) and hot chocolate (1 item) within a mixed coffee/cocoa/tea group
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Randomly purchased in Beirut market; growing origin not reported
study.sampling_unit: single retail item analysed in triplicate
study.method: FAAS (Shimadzu AA-6800), H2O2/HNO3 hot-plate digestion of 5 g fresh weight
study.lod_loq: Al LOD 0.04 ppm, LOQ 0.12 ppm (solution basis implied)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary presents 'Coffee, cocoa and tea | 6.36' as a group concentration; the text says group means were 'presented by its climax', and Fig. 1 shows the group mean near 3.5 mg/kg with a maximum near 6.3 mg/kg, so 6.36 appears to be the group maximum, not a cocoa value.
Routing to ingredients/chocolate is not supported by any chocolate-specific measurement (chocolate muffin and chocolate wafer are composite foods, out of scope).
unresolved: Item-level Al value for cocoa powder not printed anywhere in the paper; only the mixed group can be read from Fig. 1 (not cocoa-specific).
Whether 'Hot chocolate' was analysed as powder or as prepared drink is not stated.
